title: Playing the lumber and logging camps
summary: He lived and played at logging camps for room, board and wages; camps moved on flat cars; he also played surrounding towns.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You hear stories about the lumber camps and all, like a lot of the blues things are called-
I played on a lot of lumber camps, logging camps too.
You know, what would happen there? I mean, you weren't working there in the camp or anything, you'd just go there and play?

No, I was living there playing. I used to play on Barth camp for a guy they called Gold Mine. That was a logging camp. Well, I got twenty-five dollars a week room and board. I stayed on the place. Yeah. I played for Curtis Coleman and Barth in the same camp.
Where was that, up in Mississippi or Louisiana?
That was up in Mississippi. Down in Bush, Louisiana, that's down below Boagalusi, played out there on that camp for Tom Payne. A guy, he run the place by the name of Tom Payne.
At those camps, I mean, when would you play? Would they have sort of a bar room there?
Well, they'd have music practical every night. They would dance along.
Were there women around, a lot of women around the camp too, or how did that? Oh, yeah. See, I don't know anything about those long camps.
Yeah, there'd be plenty of women. There'd be some fine ones around there too. Yeah. Kind of love them. And most of them loved the dance, you know.

Yeah. A real camp, excuse me for keep talking about it since I don't know about it, I want to find out. Did they move those camps around when they, say, cut down a lot of the forest? Did they move it over? What did they have? Tents or cabins?

They had little houses, shacks like they called them. They put them up on flat cars, you know. Take a crane and pick them up. Oh, yeah. Set them up on the flat car and move them to the next place. So they'd move those around the country then? Move them around the country.
As they'd go into a new timbers actually. That's right. And then you'd stay with the camp there and just play music on every night?

Well, not exactly. Sometime I'd go to another camp or another town or go to like Bogalusi or play there. I used to play in Bogalusi too. And also I'd play around Jackson, Mississippi, Meridian, Hattiesburg, Natchez, Vicksburg, different places like that. Cholula, Louisiana, Faraday, Louisiana.
